papers.title: Necropolitics of ıntimacy: family violence and trans lives in Türkiye.
papers.abstract: This article examines the violence experienced by trans individuals in Türkiye within family and intimate relationships, treating it as a structured, enduring regime rather than a series of isolated acts. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 17 trans individuals, the study uses reflexive thematic analysis to trace how violence originates within the family and extends into intimate relationships, public spaces, and institutional encounters. The analysis brings together Agamben's state of exception and bare life with Mbembe's necropolitics and politics of enmity to show how trans individuals are excluded from legal and moral protection and governed through abandonment, exposure, and slow death. Relocating Agamben's concepts from the concentration camp, his paradigmatic site of exception, to the family, the article distinguishes domination within family membership from the revocation of membership itself and treats bare life as a negotiated asymptote rather than an inhabited condition. The findings show that violence is normalised through discourses of love, protection and morality, while state institutions often withdraw from their protective role or become sites of secondary harm. Preventing violence against trans individuals requires political interventions that simultaneously address familial relations, intimate life, and institutional responsibility.

papers.title: Certified reference materials in nuclear forensics: Foundations, applications, and future directions.
papers.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
papers.abstract: Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) are the cornerstone of traceable nuclear measurements, yet their role in nuclear forensic science has not been comprehensively reviewed. This work presents a critical analysis of existing uranium-, plutonium-, and mixed-actinide-based CRMs, highlighting their metrological design, analytical applications, and forensic relevance. Drawing on data from the IAEA, JRC-Geel, NIST, and national metrology institutes, the review delineates the evolution of CRMs from bulk isotopic standards to gravimetrically certified, radiochronometric, and micro-particulate materials relevant to nuclear forensic investigations. The study identifies persistent gaps in CRM availability for advanced fuel cycles, minor actinides, and nanoparticulate systems, which limit analytical comparability and forensic traceability. Case studies illustrate the integration of CRMs into isotope-dilution mass spectrometry and age-dating using the 241Pu-241Am chronometer, demonstrating their indispensable role in establishing data reliability and legal defensibility in nuclear forensic contexts. Beyond technical evaluation, the paper introduces a conceptual framework positioning CRMs as tools supporting both measurement accuracy and nuclear forensic interpretation. Collectively, the review outlines priorities for the next generation of nuclear forensic CRMs, linking analytical precision to nuclear security applications.

papers.title: Psychedelic Drug Use and Romantic Relationship Functioning.
papers.abstract: Romantic relationship quality is closely tied to individual outcomes, with higher quality relationships corresponding to better mental and physical health. Illicit drug use is known to associate with relationship dysfunction, however literature on this topic largely ignores or conflates psychedelics with other illicit drugs. The present study compared relationship functioning among people who reported past-year psychedelic use, stimulant/opioid use, and nonuse of illicit drugs using data from the National Couples' Health and Time Study (NCHAT). Those who indicated psychedelic use did not differ from those who indicated no drug use on most outcomes, though they reported lower commitment. Those who reported stimulant/opioid use demonstrated worse functioning than those who reported no drug use, showing lower satisfaction, worse dyadic coping, higher marital risk, more negative interactions, and higher odds of perpetrating intimate partner abuse. Between those who disclosed drug use, people who reported psychedelic use indicated fewer negative interactions and lower odds of perpetrating intimate partner abuse than people who reported stimulant/opioid use, with trends toward greater couples satisfaction and better dyadic coping. These findings suggest that people who choose to use psychedelics exhibit meaningful differences in interpersonal functioning than those who use illicit stimulants and opioids.

papers.title: New species from the cradle of biodiversity inventories: cryptic diversity within Lamellariinae in the European Atlantic and Mediterranean (Gastropoda: Velutinidae).
papers.abstract: The Mediterranean, despite a long tradition of naturalist observation dating back to Aristotle, is still home to undisclosed cryptic species complexes. The gastropod subfamily Lamellariinae d'Orbigny, 1841 (Velutinidae Gray, 1840) is composed of benthic sea slug-like species with a vestigial internal shell covered by the mantle. The high morphological plasticity of this group hampers species delimitation and identification. In the Mediterranean Sea, two - considered well-known - species are present: Lamellaria latens (O. F. Müller, 1776) and Marsenia perspicua (Linnaeus, 1758). This study assesses the real diversity of this group using an integrative taxonomy approach that combines molecular (COI, 16S rRNA, ITS2, 28S rRNA), morphological (body size, shell, radula, internal anatomy) and ecological data (geographic distribution, depth). The genus Marsenia Oken, 1823 is recognised as a synonym of Lamellaria Montagu, 1816 and the new genus Marseniotta n. gen. is established for Marsenia sensu authors. Two cryptic species complexes are recognised, in the European Atlantic and Mediterranean, with a total of six species, three here described as new: Lamellaria alba n. sp., Lamellaria violacea n. sp., and Marseniotta corsicana n. sp. Additionally, Eirenika n. gen. is proposed as a replacement name for the lamellariine genus Pacifica Fassio, Bouchet & Oliverio, 2022, which is a junior homonym. Our results suggest that characters traditionally used for species identification in this group, such as body size, shell shape and mantle colouration, are unreliable when examined across a broader dataset. Some recurrent chromatic patterns, protoconch and radula shape, can be used, in combination with geographic distribution, to attempt a first genus-level identification. However, given the high degree of plasticity and overlap in morphological characters, genetic data emerge as essential for a correct species-level identification in this group.

papers.title: Microsurgical Clipping of a Tumor-Like Bilobulated Ophthalmic Aneurysm: A 2-Dimensional Operative Video.
papers.abstract: Ophthalmic artery aneurysm are technically challenging lesions because of their complex paraclinoid anatomy and intimate relationship with the optic apparatus, internal carotid artery (ICA), and ophthalmic artery.1-3 Visual dysfunction is an important clinical presentation, particularly in large aneurysms causing optic nerve compression, and visual outcomes remain a major consideration when selecting among microsurgical and endovascular treatment strategies.4-6 Microsurgical clipping remains an important option in selected complex aneurysms because it provides definitive exclusion while allowing direct optic nerve decompression and parent-vessel reconstruction.2,4,7. We present the operative video of 59-year-old woman with progressive right-predominant visual deterioration over approximately 30 days. Imaging demonstrated a large, irregular, bilobulated ophthalmic artery aneurysm measuring 18 x 11 mm, with an 8 mm neck and postcontrast wall enhancement. Given the progressive visual deficit and optic nerve compression, microsurgical treatment was selected. Following proximal cervical ICA control and a pterional-transsylvian approach,8 the optic nerve was decompressed and the aneurysm exposed. Its broad neck and complex bilobulated morphology required tandem clip reconstruction of the ICA while preserving ophthalmic artery flow. Motor-evoked potentials and indocyanine green videoangiography guided clip adjustment. Atherosclerotic plaque at ophthalmic artery origin further influenced final clip positioning. Postoperative CTA confirmed parent-vessel patency, and visual field testing demonstrated improvement at 2 weeks. This video demonstrates optic nerve decompression, reconstructive clipping, and flow-preserving microsurgical strategies for a complex ophthalmic artery aneurysm.

papers.title: Neural coordination of wing and leg movements during a terrestrial threat display.
papers.abstract: In most flying species, legs and wings mediate earthbound vs. aerial locomotion, respectively. During terrestrial social displays such as threat or courtship, however, species-typical movements of these appendages are coordinated in a stereotyped manner. How such appendicular control is integrated is poorly understood. Threat behavior in Drosophila consists of four types of leg and wing actions, which can be performed singly or in combination. Using a large-scale functional screen, we previously identified a cluster of 4-5 AIP (CL062) neurons whose optogenetic activation can evoke all threat actions and which are essential for natural threat displays. To understand how this threat command module functions, we have mapped AIP neurons into the male fly connectome and identified split-GAL4 drivers for four major downstream targets, whose functional connectivity and behavioral roles we have tested. Surprisingly, we find that distinct threat-specific actions are not controlled by parallel connections from different subsets of AIP cells to different action-specific descending neurons (DNs), a parsimonious circuit architecture. Rather, AIP neurons collectively activate two parallel downstream modules comprising pairs of neurons that control wing vs. leg movements, respectively. Wing movements are controlled via direct projections to two specialist DNs that act synergistically, while leg movements are controlled indirectly via two interneurons that act antagonistically to pattern the activity of multiple DNs, which are likely used in other locomotor contexts. These data elucidate a hierarchical circuit for appendicular coordination during a terrestrial social display and provide insight into how the brain has repurposed appendage-specific locomotor control for social communication, a form of exaptation.

papers.title: Ancient Greek votive epigraphy: Ancient religion between individual choice and cultural trends.
papers.abstract: Ancient votive inscriptions, numbering in the tens of thousands across the Mediterranean, offer direct evidence for religious practice but have rarely been studied comprehensively across time and space due to their sheer volume. This paper presents a "distant reading" analysis of approximately 11,000 Greek dedicatory inscriptions (sixth century BCE - seventh century CE) drawn primarily from the GIST/I.PHI digital corpus. By tagging inscriptions for key features (votive/dedicatory terminology, deities, motives, gender) and analyzing their distribution chronologically and geographically while controlling for the "epigraphic habit," this study identifies large-scale trends. The results reveal a significant relative increase in the use of explicit votive terminology (forms of euche/euchomai) over time, particularly during the Roman Imperial period and Late Antiquity. This practice exhibits strong regional variation, being markedly more prevalent in Asia Minor and the East than in mainland Greece before the fourth century CE. Furthermore, the use of votive formulae correlates strongly with specific deities (e.g., Men, Meter, Hypsistos, Hosios kai Dikaios) and negatively with others (e.g., emperors, Athena). Votive terminology also appears negatively correlated with the explicit mention of other motives (like dreams or commands) and with the use of standard consecration terms. While demonstrating the potential of computational methods for identifying broad patterns of continuity and change in religious expression, the study also highlights methodological challenges (dating uncertainty, data tagging) and underscores the persistent difficulty in definitively separating shifts in epigraphic conventions from changes in underlying religious mentalities.

papers.title: Radiocarbon dating of wooden beams at Herodium palace-fortress: Modeling tree-felling events and their implications on site chronology.
papers.abstract: The site of Herodium is best known for its impressive, well-preserved palace fortress, built by Herod the Great, towards the end of the 1st century BC. The site's conical shape, artificially created to transform it into Herod's monumental burial complex, is clearly seen from afar. The impressive preservation of wooden beams and posts at the site has allowed for a rigorous radiocarbon study of the beams' felling dates and their potential implications for the timing of construction activities at the site. A total of 24 14C measurements were performed on specific growth rings from 11 beams and posts, associated with six (sub) phases at the site. This level of detail, combined with Bayesian modeling and sensitivity testing of potential seasonal offsets, has revealed that the wood used at the site originates from four main tree-felling events. Apparently, the first event might have been as early as Alexander Jannaeus's time, in the first quarter of the 1st century BC - a period not currently identified in the archaeological record at the site. The second reflects an extensive supply of wood, felled during the period corresponding to the beginning of the main phase of Herod's massive construction activity (40-30 BC, approximately), followed by a possible third felling event towards the end of Herod's life or shortly after. The fourth felling event was identified in beams used during the Bar-Kokhba revolt in 132-136 AD. However, the beams were felled several decades earlier, around 100 AD, between the Great Revolt (66-71 AD) and the Bar-Kokhba one, in a period characterized by limited documented occupation, indicating that the wood was used several decades after the trees were felled. The origin of some of those beams is probably from the extensive gardens Herod planted at the site.

papers.title: Perceptions of relationship changes during pregnancy in Latinas: A qualitative study.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Pregnancy is shaped by complex social dynamics and interpersonal changes that influence how expecting mothers connect with their families and others around them. While social support has been linked to better maternal mental health, less is known about how relationships themselves change during pregnancy. This study explores how pregnant Latinas living in the United States perceive changes in their family, partner, and peer relationships and how these evolving connections influence their sense of support. A subset of 48 pregnant Latinas who participated in a larger study took part in a one-on-one interview conducted in English or Spanish. Participants were recruited from community-based and institutional settings. Thematic analysis revealed three key themes and six subthemes. First, participants described strengthened maternal bonds with their own mothers and other close family members, along with increased relatability with other pregnant women. Second, participants often reported social withdrawal and isolation. This was driven by pregnancy symptoms, exclusion from social activities, and changes in how others treated them as a result of the pregnancy. Third, participants described varied changes in romantic relationship dynamics, including increased emotional distance for some, stability for others, and a desire for greater partner involvement. This study highlights the role of interpersonal relationships in shaping Latina's pregnancy experiences. Changes in family relationships, especially with maternal figures, as well as with partners and peers, influenced participants' emotional well-being and belonging during pregnancy. These findings highlight the need to consider relational dynamics in support efforts for Latinas and their families. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Friend or Foe: The Use of Cannabis as a Potential Analgesic in Postoperative Lumbar Spine Surgery.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
papers.abstract: Cannabis is a plant-based product which has been documented in medicinal usage dating back nearly 5000 years ago in 400 AD. With time, cannabis would come to become the most grown, cultivated, trafficked, and abused illicit drug worldwide. As a result, cannabis became a schedule 1 substance having no accepted medical use. In 1996, however, cannabis emerged in the medicinal scene when California became the first state to allow legal access to cannabis for medicinal purposes under the Compassionate Use Act. As of November 8, 2023, 24 states, two territories, and the District of Columbia all enacted laws to help regulate not only the use of marijuana medicinally but recreational use as well. A large proponent for the shift regarding the utilization of medicinal cannabis occurred as a direct result of the opioid abuse crisis which came to fruition in the late 1990s due to their outstanding ability to mitigate the human kryptonite; Pain. The goal of the present literature review is to better consolidate and critically think about the usage of cannabis perioperatively and its utility as a postoperative pain mitigator. More so, many current review articles, systematic reviews, and retrospective reviews suggest deleterious effects of the patient population undergoing lumbar spine surgery who also engage in cannabis usage. However, a lack of level I evidence continues to exist surrounding the clinical question of cannabis usage as a perioperative pain mitigator, leading to inconclusive recommendations regarding its utility. The present review aims to highlight the multitude of conflicting research and identify gaps in questions, which may lead to better utilization and recognition of cannabis as either a helpful or hurtful pain remedy.

papers.title: Genome evolution of Mediterranean olives following DNA repeats diversification.
papers.abstract: The olive tree (Olea europaea L. subsp. europaea) is one of the most representative perennial crops of the Mediterranean Basin, yet the genomic processes underlying its domestication and diversification remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated repeatome variation across 20 accessions, including 11 wild oleasters and nine cultivated varieties, using comparative clustering of high-throughput sequencing data, complemented by structural analyses of transposable elements (TEs) and tandem repeats (TRs). Repetitive DNA accounts for about 54% of the olive genomes and is composed primarily of long terminal repeat retrotransposons (LTR-REs) and TRs. Comparative analyses revealed lineage-specific differences in LTR-REs between wild and cultivated genotypes, while TRs exhibited higher abundances and greater variability in oleasters for some families (e.g., Oe-80 and Oe-178), reinforcing the view that TRs evolve rapidly and largely independently in olive. We also identified a new TR (Oe-155) and confirmed its distinct monomer sequence and chromosomal organization, suggesting that this subfamily is differentiating from TRs Oe-218 and Oe-80. To refine TE dynamics, we surveyed full-length elements in two reference assemblies (cv. Leccino and a wild sylvestris genotype). Leccino is enriched in intact LTR-REs, whereas sylvestris harbored more full-length Class II DNA transposons. Additionally, the patterns of TE-gene proximity vary significantly between them. Dating of full-length LTR-RE insertions revealed that most RE activity predates domestication, with only a small fraction of very recent insertions. These results highlight repetitive DNA as a major contributor to genome diversification in olive and provide a foundation for integrating repeatome variation with demographic history, introgression, and clonal propagation. The olive tree is a key crop in the Mediterranean region, but the genetic processes that shaped its diversity and domestication remain poorly understood. I

papers.title: Nutritional Care in Traditional Mongolian Medicine: Historical Foundations and Conceptual Framework Development-A Historical Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Nutritional care has long been a fundamental component of Traditional Mongolian Medicine (TMM), reflecting a holistic understanding of health, diet, and disease prevention. This study aimed to examine the historical and conceptual foundations of nutritional care in TMM and to develop a conceptual framework based on historical TMM texts. METHODS: Historical research was conducted using Berg's seven-stage historical research framework and primary TMM texts dating from the sixth to the twentieth centuries. Recurrent concepts related to food, beverages, nutrition, and health maintenance were identified and analyzed through concept analysis. The resulting concepts were synthesized using concept mapping to develop a conceptual framework of nutritional care in TMM. RESULTS: Historical analysis revealed the progressive development and refinement of nutritional knowledge throughout the evolution of TMM. Five recurrent concepts were identified: cosmological foundations of nourishment, bodily balance and humoral regulation, dietary classification, contextualized nutritional assessment, and therapeutic nutritional care. These concepts were integrated into a conceptual framework structured around four interrelated domains: nutritional assessment, planning, intervention, and evaluation. CONCLUSION: This study provides a systematic conceptualization of nutritional care grounded in TMM and proposes a framework that organizes its historical principles into a coherent model. The framework offers a foundation for future empirical studies examining the application and relevance of TMM-based nutritional care in contemporary healthcare contexts.

papers.title: Investigations on the delamination mechanism of double-glass photovoltaic modules based on laser treating.
papers.abstract: The growing number of decommissioned photovoltaic (PV) modules calls for efficient recycling methods with minimal material damage. This study developed a preheating-assisted pulsed laser strategy for interfacial delamination of double-glass crystalline silicon PV modules and investigated the underlying mechanisms. Preheating softened the EVA encapsulant and broadened the laser-processing window, although preheating alone was insufficient to induce EVA/Si delamination. Among the investigated conditions, a heater setpoint of 200 °C provided the widest stable-delamination window. The laser beam passed through the top glass and upper EVA encapsulant with limited optical loss and was predominantly absorbed by silicon. Four characteristic states emerged with increasing laser energy density: non-separable, difficult-to-delaminate, stable delamination, and carbonized delamination. Interfacial weakening involved coupled responses of EVA, the SiNx antireflection layer, and the silicon surface. EVA deacetylation reduced the abundance of polar ester groups and weakened chemical adhesion, while damage to the SiNx layer and localized silicon melting-resolidification altered the interfacial bonding environment and reduced mechanical interlocking. Transient pressure from localized vaporization and volatile-product release may have further assisted crack propagation across regions where the pyramidal texture remained intact. These coupled effects enabled relatively continuous EVA/Si delamination with limited material damage. Excessive energy input caused EVA carbonization, severe surface ablation, and silicon fracture. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for process optimization and low-damage recovery of materials from double-glass PV modules.

papers.title: Aptamer-grafted amino-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for simultaneous exceptional selectivity and high-capacity adsorption of four aflatoxins.
papers.abstract: Precise quantification of aflatoxins in complex food matrices remains challenging because of substantial matrix interference. In this work, an aptamer-grafted amino-functionalized covalent organic framework (Apt@NH2-COF) was developed through covalent immobilization of aptamers using a heterobifunctional crosslinker. The introduced aptamers significantly enhanced analyte-specific molecular recognition, enabling highly selective adsorption of aflatoxins B1, B2, G1, and G2, with corresponding adsorption capacities of 23.05, 15.92, 21.50, and 16.39 mg g-1, respectively. Experimental investigations combined with density functional theory calculations and molecular docking revealed that adsorption was governed by the synergistic effects of electron donor-acceptor hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, and hydrophobic interactions, with the immobilized aptamers providing analyte-specific recognition and the COF scaffold ensuring high-capacity enrichment. When employed as the solid-phase extraction sorbent coupled with UPLC-MS/MS, the proposed method enabled simultaneous determination of four aflatoxins with wide linear ranges (0.02-10.0 ng g-1), low limits of detection (0.002-0.022 ng g-1), satisfactory recoveries (80.8%-112.5%), and good reusability over 12 adsorption-desorption cycles. Overall, the proposed Apt@NH2-COF provides an effective affinity sorbent for selective aflatoxin enrichment and offers a feasible strategy for improving sample preparation in complex food matrices.

papers.title: Enhancing the stability and solubility of esculetin by cucurbit[n]uril (n = 6-8) encapsulation: A computational study to identify the Ideal host.
papers.abstract: Esculetin (Eu) is a naturally occurring secondary metabolite with ethnopharmacological significance and is widely used as an anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and anticancer drug, but it has poor aqueous solubility. To address this limitation, this study explores encapsulating Eu within cucurbit[n]urils (n = 6-8) using density functional theory (DFT) methods and evaluates the resulting structure, stability, and electronic properties. DFT calculations at the Domain-based Local Pair Natural Orbital Coupled-Cluster with Singles, Doubles, and perturbative Triples, DLPNO-CCSD(T)/def2-SVP//M06-2X-D3/6-31G(d) method revealed that CB[6] forms a more stable complex with Eu than CB[7] and CB[8]. Thermodynamic parameters confirm the formation of the inclusion complexes, with a larger Gibbs free energy and enthalpy change for the Eu complex with CB[6] than for the other studied inclusion complexes. Frontier orbitals and their energy gaps show that the complexes share similar features with Eu. Noncovalent interaction analysis (NCI) and Independent Gradient Model (IGM) analyses showed hydrogen bonding between the phenolic group of Eu and CB[n], with a cooperative effect of van der Waals interactions predominantly in the Eu@CB[6] complex. Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM), Dispersion Interaction Density (DID), and Local Energy Decomposition (LED) analyses show that hydrogen bonding between Eu and the carbonyl portal of CBs plays a major role in stabilization, with a significant attractive electrostatic contribution, followed by dispersion and exchange terms. LED analysis shows that Eu@CB[6] has the highest preparation energy, followed by the dispersion interaction, while the DID analysis shows a continuous dispersion density around the carbonyl portal. Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics show that Eu remains inside the cavity throughout the simulation for CB[6] and CB[8], whereas in CB[7] the guest gets expelled from the cavity. papers.title: Crystal structure of the rhombohedral vacancy-ordered perovskite (CH3NH3)2[SnCl6] for deep-UV optoelectronic applications.
papers.abstract: Lead-free zero-dimensional (0D) hybrid halide perovskites A2SnX6 are promising candidates for stable deep-UV optoelectronics; however, the chloride end-members of the series remain underexplored. This study presents a comprehensive structural, optical, and electrical characterization of the vacancy-ordered hybrid hexachlorostannate, (CH3NH3)2[SnCl6], synthesized via controlled slow evaporation. Single crystal X-ray diffraction, combined with Raman spectroscopy, shows that this hybrid halide has a trigonal structure (space group R3̄m) composed of isolated [SnCl6]2- octahedra dynamically coupled to methylammonium cations via a robust N-H⋯Cl hydrogen-bonding network. Optical absorption analysis reveals behaviour characteristic of wide-bandgap semiconductor, dominated by ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) transitions. Tauc and Urbach analyses yield a direct optical bandgap of ∼3.54 eV and an Urbach energy of 0.17 eV, highlighting the role of dynamic cation disorder in broadening the absorption edge. Furthermore, temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy (323-413 K) demonstrates thermally activated small-polaron hopping. The AC conductivity is rigorously described by the Correlated Barrier Hopping (CBH) model (W M = 0.201 eV, E a = 0.30 eV). The frequency exponent decreases monotonically with temperature, confirming that charge transport is governed by coulombically correlated hopping between localized Sn-centered states, heavily modulated by grain boundary resistance and organic sublattice dynamics. These findings establish (CH3NH3)2[SnCl6] as a structurally robust, lead-free reference material, offering a tunable platform for deep-UV photodetection and wavelength-selective optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Tuning σ‑Hole Chalcogen···Nitrogen Bonding Between C2F4Ch2 and Nitrogen Bases: Dual Modulation by Chalcogen Atomic Size and Nitrogen Hybridization (Ch = S, Se, Te, Po).
papers.abstract: Chalcogen bonds (ChBs), a prominent subclass of σ-hole interactions in which Group 16 elements serve as electrophilic sites, have attracted considerable attention in recent years because of their pivotal roles in diverse chemical and biological systems. However, the combined influence of the chalcogen atomic size and the nitrogen atomic hybridization state on the nature and strength of chalcogen···nitrogen (Ch···N) interactions remains underexplored. Herein, σ-hole-type Ch···N ChBs formed between 2,2,4,4-tetrafluoro-1,3-dichalcogenetanes (C2F4Ch2, Ch = S, Se, Te, Po) and nitrogen bases with distinct hybridization patterns (sp-NCH, sp2-NHCH2, sp2-pyridine, sp3-NH3) are systematically investigated using quantum chemical calculations. The computed interaction energies vary from -16.8 to -62.5 kJ/mol. The two moieties are held together primarily through the Ch···N ChBs. These ChBs show substantial bond contraction, with Ch···N distances approximately 12-29% shorter than the sum of the respective van der Waals radii. Topological analysis indicates that although most Ch···N ChBs exhibit noncovalent closed-shell characteristics, Te/Po···N ChBs in complexes with NH3, NHCH2, or pyridine display a partially covalent nature. Notably, the Ch···N ChB strength typically increases in the order Ch = S < Se < Po < Te and follows the nitrogen base sequence: NCH (sp) < NH3 (sp3) < NHCH2 (sp2) < pyridine (sp2). Natural bond orbital (NBO) analysis suggests that the predominant orbital interaction associated with the Ch···N ChB involves charge transfer from the nitrogen lone pair into the σ*-(C-Ch) antibonding orbitals. papers.title: Relationship Quality Among Married Indian Couples: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Indian marriages have traditionally been understood as fulfilling religious commitments, forming alliances between families and fostering companionship between spouses. However, relationship quality in such marriages is shaped by structural and cultural factors that Western models of marriage, which consider only the dyadic relationship, do not account for. This narrative review examines relationship quality among married Indian couples across three themes: caste and joint-family structure; communication and conflict; and intimacy, identity and sexual satisfaction, to understand how relationship quality is shaped beyond the couple. SUMMARY: The review draws on attachment theory, social exchange theory and family systems theory, as well as on indigenous Indian thought and the feminist bargaining-power framework of Sen and Agarwal, alongside broader cultural and philosophical perspectives. It considers how structure and individual agency combine in the process of Indian marriage, drawing on narrative, empirical, theoretical, economic and philosophical sources, as well as Indian legal decisions. Caste and kinship structure a wife's bargaining power and household authority before dyadic interactions occur; communication and conflict are shaped by joint-family privacy rather than the dyad alone; and emotional intimacy and identity shape relationship quality, while sexual satisfaction remains comparatively unexplored in the Indian context. The review proposes two original theoretical constructs, active endurance, which extends Das's notion of endurance, and the aspiration-structure gap, to capture patterns evident in the literature but not yet formally theorised. It also notes neurobiological evidence, namely hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation in chronic marital distress and oxytocin's modulation of couple conflict, which warrants investigation in Indian samples. KEY MESSAGE: Therapy and policy addressing relationship quality in Indian marriages

papers.title: Construction of photo-activated berberine-rhein self-assembled nanoparticle/gelatin-chitosan composite films and their antibacterial performance.
papers.abstract: To address the persistent environmental burden of petroleum-based plastics and the intrinsic limitations of natural biopolymer films, this study developed an enhanced active packaging material (GC/BR composite film) via the strategic incorporation of self-assembled berberine-rhein nanoparticles (BR NPs) into a gelatin/chitosan (GC) hybrid matrix. Molecular dynamics simulations coupled with various spectroscopic analyses revealed that the co-assembly of BR NPs was primarily stabilized by robust π-π stacking, electrostatic interactions, and hydrogen bonding. The reinforcement effect of BR NPs is attributed to their uniform dispersion and interfacial interactions with the GC matrix, which facilitate efficient stress transfer. As a result, the composite film exhibits notable mechanical enhancements relative to the pure GC film: tensile strength increases by 62% and elongation at break by 88%, accompanied by an improved water vapor barrier. Notably, the GC/BR film retained the aggregation-induced emission characteristics of the photosensitizer, and exhibited effective photodynamic sterilization upon visible-light irradiation. In vitro antibacterial assays demonstrated 100% inactivation against Staphylococcus aureus and 99% against Escherichia coli within 20 min of visible-light irradiation. Real-food preservation trials using chicken breasts further validated the film's capacity to suppress microbial proliferation. Crucially, migration tests revealed a maximum BR NPs leachate concentration of 0.0032 mg/mL (60-fold lower than the highest concentration in hemolysis assays), suggesting a low migration risk and a favorable preliminary biosafety profile. This work provides a promising strategy for the rational design of robust, biodegradable active packaging materials with integrated photodynamic functionality.

papers.title: Restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks via hydroxyl-functionalized covalent organic frameworks for efficient nitrate electroreduction.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) is a promising strategy for nitrate removal and ammonia synthesis, but its efficiency is largely limited by sluggish proton transfer kinetics and poor reaction selectivity. Herein, we rationally design a series of hydroxyl-functionalized copper phthalocyanine-based covalent organic frameworks (Cu-COF-nOH) to regulate interfacial proton transfer via restructuring hydrogen-bonding networks. The hydroxyl functional groups in Cu-COF-nOH enhance water adsorption and dissociation to enrich interfacial proton supply. Optimized hydroxyl loading further induces the formation of continuous hydrogen-bond chains, enabling oriented and accelerated proton shuttling toward Cu active centers instead of stochastic diffusion. Electrocatalytic tests in 0.5 M nitrate electrolyte show that the optimal Cu-COF-4OH catalyst achieves an ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 93.20% and an NH3 yield rate of 65.84 mg·h-1, along with excellent long-term stability, outperforming most state-of-the-art NO3RR electrocatalysts. Combined with in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations, we clearly clarify that hydroxyl-mediated hydrogen-bonding restructuring plays a critical role in boosting proton transfer kinetics and reaction selectivity. This work provides a versatile interface engineering strategy for efficient multiproton/electron-coupled electrocatalytic reactions, offering insights into the design of high-performance NO3RR catalysts.

papers.title: Strain induced phase transitions, superior optoelectronics, and photocatalytic potential of Ba2GdNbO6: promising material for solar hydrogen production.
papers.abstract: Strain engineering provides an effective route for tuning the multifunctional features of materials, thereby enhancing their potential for spintronic and energy-conversion applications. In this work, we investigate the effects of hydrostatic ([111]) strain on the structural, mechanical, magnetic, electronic, photocatalytic, and optical aspects of the Ba2GdNbO6 structure using first-principles calculations within GGA + U (generalized gradient approximation + Hubbard parameter) and GGA + U + SOC (spin-orbit coupling) frameworks. The negative formation enthalpies, elastic constants, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations confirm the thermodynamic, mechanical, and thermal stability of the structures. Further, vibrational free-energy calculations reveal that tensile strain becomes thermodynamically favorable at elevated temperatures due to enhanced vibrational entropy. It is predicted that unstrained compound exhibits an indirect band gap (E g) of 3.27/3.26 eV with a stable ferromagnetic (FM) ground state within the GGA + U/GGA + U + SOC scheme. Interestingly, under compressive strain, a magnetic transition from the FM to antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state occurs, accompanied by an electronic indirect-to-direct E g transition. In contrast, tensile strains preserve the FM ground state having lower indirect E g as is found in the unstrained one. Moreover, charge-density, electron localization function, and Bader analyses reveal enhanced metal-oxygen charge transfer under compression and reduced orbital overlap under tension while preserving predominantly ionic bonding. Notably, the system exhibits near ultraviolet light-harvesting, achieving absorption coefficients as high as 1.26/1.18/1.10 × 106 cm-1 at 3.26 eV, 1.48/1.44/1.42 × 106 cm-1 3.26 eV, and 1.36/1.37/1.36 × 106 cm-1 2.87 eV along the xx-/yy-/zz-axis for the -5%, 0%, and +5% strained systems, respectively, highlighting its excellent optical response. papers.title: Achieving record birefringence in metal-free semiorganic sulfate crystals via tetrahedral anionic group substitution.
papers.abstract: Birefringent crystals with the ability to precisely modulate polarized light are indispensable optical devices in modern optics and optoelectronics. However, achieving high birefringence in such crystals remains a challenge. Integration of the π-conjugated 2-amino-5-methylpyridine (AMPy), which has large polarizability anisotropy, with non-π-conjugated tetrahedral groups produces two birefringent crystals, AMPy·PO4 and AMPy·SO4. AMPy·PO4 has a three-dimensional hydrogen-bonding structure, whereas AMPy·SO4 exhibits a two-dimensional hydrogen-bonded layer. Remarkably, upon substituting phosphate with sulfate, the experimental birefringence increases 3.8-fold, yielding a giant birefringence of 0.506 at 550 nm coupled with broad optical transparency and establishing AMPy·SO4 as a new benchmark for metal-free sulfate crystals. Structural and computational investigations reveal that the outstanding birefringence of AMPy·SO4 mainly originates from two key factors: the formation of a layered structure where tetrahedral sulfate anions modulate the arrangement of optically anisotropic AMPy cations to achieve nearly parallel alignment via hydrogen bonding, and the dense stacking of planar π-conjugated AMPy moieties. This work not only offers a universal strategy for designing semiorganic birefringent crystals via synergistically combining π-conjugated groups and non-π-conjugated rigid tetrahedral moieties but also pushes the birefringence limit of metal-free sulfate crystals to a new level.

papers.title: Homoleptic teflate coordination at platinum(iv): synthesis and characterization of [Pt(OTeF5)6]2-, and covalency trends revealed by the OSLO method.
papers.abstract: The pentafluoroorthotellurate group (teflate, -OTeF5) is a unique ligand in transition metal and main group chemistry that combines exceptionally strong electron-withdrawing properties, comparable to those of fluorine, with substantial steric demand. However, its coordination behaviour in transition metal complexes remains poorly understood, in part due to the scarcity of homoleptic transition metal teflate complexes, particularly for late transition metals. By reacting [NEt4]2[PtCl6] and ClOTeF5 under solvent-free conditions, we have synthesized the first hexacoordinate homoleptic transition-metal teflate complex, [NEt4]2[Pt(OTeF5)6]. This compound exhibits an extraordinary stability: it is bench-stable, resistant toward hydrolysis and alcoholysis, and displays a high thermal decomposition temperature of 200 °C. In the crystallographically determined molecular structure, the O-Te bond lengths, together with the ν(O-Te) stretching vibration in the IR spectrum, point toward a pronounced covalent contribution in the Pt-O interaction. To better understand the bonding situation and the electronic stucture of the complex, the system was further analysed using energy decomposition analysis coupled with natural orbitals for chemical valence (EDA-NOCV), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) and the oxidation state localized orbital (OSLO) method. The latter unambiguously assigns an oxidation state of +IV to the platinum centre. A linear correlation between the fragment orbital localization index (FOLI) value of the M-O σ bonding orbital of various homoleptic metal teflate complexes and their experimentally determined mean O-Te bond length was identified. This relationship was subsequently extended to homoleptic main-group teflate compounds, highlighting the general applicability of this approach for assessing the nature of element-teflate bonds.

papers.title: Lactate dehydrogenase A-dependent redox control of selective mRNA translation directs monocyte fate commitment.
papers.abstract: Monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation is a central process that shapes immune responses across diverse contexts, yet how inflammatory cues engage metabolism to instruct monocyte fate commitment remains unclear. Here, using a CRISPR-based metabolic screen combined with monocyte-specific perturbations in bacterial lung infection, we identified lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) as a key metabolic regulator of monocyte commitment to the nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2)+ macrophage fate in vivo. LDHA-dependent cytosolic nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) regeneration enabled selective hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1α) translation through its 5' untranslated region (UTR) and is associated with structural remodeling of this region. HIF1α then functioned as a downstream effector that promoted the NOS2+ macrophage fate. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) further acted as an upstream metabolic priming signal that enhanced LDHA-dependent HIF1α regulation and supported this differentiation process. Together, these findings suggest that metabolic redox state regulates monocyte fate commitment through selective mRNA translation coupled to RNA structural remodeling.

papers.title: Partner Dyads to Promote Physical Activity among Women at Risk for CVD: Daily Perceptions of Communication and Associations with Physical Activity Outcomes.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine day-to-day experiences of social support and peer partner influence during a tailored physical activity (PA) intervention. METHODS: The parent intervention was designed for women in midlife (ages 40-65) with elevated risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD), for whom lack of social support is a barrier to cardioprotective levels of PA. Women in midlife with ≥1 CVD risk factor (e.g., hypertension; N=62, MAge=53, MBMI=32.6 kg/m2, 44% from underrepresented groups) enrolled in an 8-week PA intervention combining PA coaching with formation of partner dyads for between-session support (n=31).Women who enrolled were paired in partner dyads and did not have a relationship prior to enrolling. They wore a digital PA monitor and completed daily end-of-day surveys throughout the program (94% compliance). Multilevel models tested for within-person associations between daily satisfaction with partner support (individual and dyad levels), including preliminary tests of partner influence. RESULTS: Partners communicated on 58% of days, primarily via texting (used on 92% of communication days). Perceived support varied within-person and within-dyad (ICCs=0.37-0.48); women reported greater PA motivation and took more steps on days when they experienced greater partner support (Ps<0.040, srs=0.19-0.32). Partners' daily PA motivation and steps showed weak correlations (rs=0.008-0.24); associations between partners' perceptions and each others' PA outcomes were slightly stronger (srs=0.20-0.28) and reflected different experiences of support. CONCLUSIONS: Among women with elevated risk for CVD, support in health-focused partnerships has potential to influence daily PA motivation and behavior. Additional investigation will improve partner-based PA intervention toward reduction in CVD risk for this group.

papers.title: Multifunctional pDA@MXene-enriched silk fibroin/PLLA nanofibrous scaffold with local piezoresponse for neural tissue engineering.
papers.journal: Journal of biomaterials science. Polymer edition
papers.abstract: Neural tissue engineering requires functional scaffolds that provide structural support while presenting biomimetic physicochemical cues to cells. Incorporating stimulus-responsive functionality into electrospun scaffolds has emerged as a promising strategy for developing next-generation neural tissue engineering platforms. In this study, a polydopamine (pDA)@MXene-enriched silk fibroin/poly(L-lactic acid) (SF/PLLA) electrospun nanofibrous scaffold was developed as a multifunctional platform for neural tissue engineering. Structural and physicochemical characterization verified the formation of Ti3C2 MXene from the Ti3AlC2 MAX precursor, successful pDA functionalization, and effective vacuum-assisted incorporation of pDA@ Ti3C2 MXenes onto the SF/PLLA nanofibrous scaffold. PFM analysis revealed a detectable local electromechanical response, consistent with the piezo-responsive characteristics of the developed scaffold. Moreover, pDA@MXene incorporation enhanced the surface hydrophilicity, as evidenced by the decrease in water contact angle from 73.49 ± 0.73° to 47.38 ± 0.6°. In-vitro experiments showed that the developed scaffold supported PC-12 cell metabolic activity throughout the culture period. SEM observations revealed effective attachment and close cell-nanofiber interactions. Under NGF-treated conditions, following a commonly used 7-day PC12 differentiation period, βIII-tubulin-positive cells with neuron-like morphological features were observed on the pDA@MXene-enriched scaffold, supporting its compatibility with NGF-induced neuronal-like phenotypic development. Collectively, the pDA@MXene-enriched scaffold exhibited enhanced surface hydrophilicity, favorable mechanical properties, local electromechanical responsiveness, and cytocompatibility, supporting its potential as a multifunctonal platform for further investigation in neural tissue engineering.

papers.title: Reward learning in prolonged grief: Evidence from the probabilistic reward task.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deficits in reward processing have been proposed as a mechanism contributing to the persistence of prolonged grief disorder (PGD). The probabilistic reward task (PRT) is a well-validated behavioural paradigm for examining reward learning. In this study, we used the PRT to investigate whether reward learning is affected in bereaved adults with probable PGD compared to bereaved controls. METHOD: Bereaved adults with probable PGD (n = 55) and bereaved controls (n = 56) completed the PRT. Reward learning was assessed using signal detection indices, reaction time (RT) distribution analyses, and hierarchical drift diffusion modelling (HDDM) to quantify latent decision parameters. Associations with prolonged grief severity and anhedonia were examined. RESULTS: Participants with probable PGD responded more slowly but did not differ reliably from bereaved controls in response bias, discriminability, accuracy, or HDDM parameters. Grief severity and hedonic capacity were not associated with task performance. CONCLUSION: The findings did not indicate a broad deficit in learning from probabilistic monetary reinforcement among participants with probable PGD. Future research should examine whether reward-related difficulties in prolonged grief are more evident in valuation or motivation, particularly for social and attachment-related rewards.

papers.title: Mediators and Moderators of Treatment Outcome Following Online Mindfulness and Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment for Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder.
papers.abstract: eSense is a digital tool delivering mindfulness-based therapy (MBT) and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to individuals with female sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD). eSense is feasible, usable, satisfying, and efficacious, and helps overcome barriers to care. We sought to examine potential mediators and moderators of improvements in sexual desire and distress following use of eSense. Women with SIAD (n = 129, mean age 44.8 ± 12.3 in the MBT arm and 41.9 ± 13.1 in the CBT arm) were randomly assigned to arm and completed self-report measures at baseline, mid-treatment, immediately post-treatment, and 6-month follow-up. Potential mediators were changes in depression, posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms (PTSD), and avoidance of sexual activity. We examined treatment expectations after module 1 as a potential moderator, and partner involvement, homework completion, and modules completed as process indicators that may predict magnitude of improvement. Decreases in depressive and PTSD symptoms were associated with improvements in sexual desire and distress in the MBT arm, and reductions in sexual avoidance were associated with improvements in both arms. Higher expectations for treatment were associated with greater improvements in desire and distress for those in the CBT arm only, whereas partner involvement, homework completion, and number of eSense modules completed were associated with improvements in both arms. This study helps identify putative mechanisms by which digital health tools for SIAD, like eSense, may be effective, and to identify participant characteristics as well as treatment engagement factors that might be associated with differential responses to online MBT and CBT.

papers.title: Intimate Partner Violence and Suicide Risk among Women Presenting to Emergency Departments: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Narrative Synthesis.
papers.abstract: Women experiencing intimate partner violence (IPV) and suicide frequently present to emergency departments (EDs). While IPV and suicide are known to co-occur, there is a limited understanding of the intersection in ED presentations. This systematic review, meta-analysis, and narrative synthesis aimed to quantify the association between IPV and suicidality in women presenting to EDs and examine the factors that influence women's suicide risk. Systematic searches of three databases identified 20 ED studies of 7,498 women, reporting associations between IPV and suicidal presentations (final search: 30 August 2025). Pooled prevalence and risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using five random-effects meta-analysis models, stratified by IPV type and suicide-related outcome. Narrative synthesis was used to examine factors associated with suicide risk. Study risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. On average, 22% (95% CI [0.11, 0.36]) of women with suicide presentations had experienced physical IPV, while 13% [0.08, 0.18] of women with IPV histories reported suicidality. IPV was associated with a three-fold increased risk of suicide attempt (RR 3.00 [1.39, 6.47]), and psychological IPV demonstrated a stronger association (RR 3.23 [1.68, 6.19]) than physical IPV (RR 2.00 [1.26, 3.17]). High between-study heterogeneity was observed across all models (I2 > 75%), and a high risk of bias was identified in half of the studies. The robust associations detected between IPV and suicide attempt underscore the need for contextualised assessment within trauma-informed emergency care to strengthen clinical response and care pathways for women.

papers.title: Developing a Strengths-Based, Culturally Grounded Intervention for Black Women Living With HIV and Intimate Partner Violence: A Formative Study of 1MoreStep.
papers.journal: The Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care : JANAC
papers.abstract: Black women in the United States face intersecting challenges of HIV and intimate partner violence. Few programs integrate safety planning with HIV care engagement while addressing strengths and contextual factors that sustain resilience. We developed 1MoreStep, a strengths-based intervention grounded in a cognitive behavioral approach and an HIV stigma framework. Formative work included 12 in-depth interviews, seven focus groups, and a six-member Community Advisory Board. Findings revealed multilevel barriers, including internalized and anticipated stigma, isolation, and structural service gaps. These insights informed a six-session hybrid curriculum incorporating cognitive behavioral tools, peer support, scenario-based activities, and the myPlan app. Guided by participants' feedback, we iteratively refined materials to ensure cultural fit, clarity, fidelity, and flexibility. 1MoreStep targets the psychological, interpersonal, and structural challenges faced by Black women living with HIV who experience intimate partner violence. A randomized, pilot, clinical trial is underway to examine the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the intervention.

papers.title: Scoping Review of Lessons Learned During the Pandemic to Improve Intimate Partner Violence Services.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic restricted access to intimate partner violence (IPV) support systems, increased the risk of IPV, and worsened already complex social and safety issues for survivors. As shelters were forced by public health mandates to adapt the way services were provided, many implemented innovative approaches to delivering care. The purpose of this unregistered review is to describe some of these adaptations and how they can continue to support survivors in a post-pandemic environment. We reviewed 261 identified reports and articles from 2018 to 2022 that were open access or available as full-text sources and included information on the impacts of COVID-19 on IPV and survivors as well as service adaptation. Inclusion criteria also required peer review and that the focus be on the U.S. population, narrowing the scope to 112 final sources. Search terms captured recommendations for different racial and ethnic groups and thematic coding revealed developments in providing services to different communities, within movement and space restrictions, and via telehealth. Researchers overwhelmingly support universal violence screening and education, especially among healthcare providers, and training in trauma-informed care. Many also endorse a community-based approach to violence prevention and service provision that engages multiple sectors and shifts the role of shelters to emergencies only. Lessons learned during the pandemic and new approaches to providing support to survivors of violence, such as telehealth, community collaboration, housing first models, and mobile advocacy, should continue to be studied to show effective avenues for implementation.

papers.title: Correction to "Maternal sensitivity and child behavior problems in the context of intimate partner violence" by Marvin et al. (2026).
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Reports an error in "Maternal sensitivity and child behavior problems in the context of intimate partner violence" by Matthew J. Marvin, Amy K. Nuttall, G. Anne Bogat, Joseph S. Lonstein, Cecilia Martinez-Torteya, Maria Muzik and Alytia A. Levendosky (Journal of Family Psychology, Advanced Online Publication, Aug 10, 2026, np; see record 2028-10690-001). In the article, there was an error when CBCL scores were calculated. Affected rows of Tables 2 and 3 provided in the erratum report these corrections. Also, in the second paragraph of the Results section, the association of the interaction between postnatal IPV and maternal sensitivity and child externalizing behavior was previously non-significant (β = -.19, p = .08) but is now significant (β = -.21, p = .04), as hypothesized. Corrected Figure 2 now depicts regions of significance for that significant interaction. The fifth paragraph of the Discussion section should have discussed the buffering effect of maternal sensitivity for both internalizing and externalizing behaviors and concluded that maternal sensitivity can be a factor that buffers the effect of postnatal IPV on internalizing along with externalizing behaviors. (The following abstract of the original article appeared in record 2028-10690-001). Intimate partner violence (IPV) is defined as physical, sexual, or psychological violence perpetrated by a romantic partner. When IPV occurs prenatally, it can affect the developing stress regulatory system of the fetus and confer risk for later behavior problems. Postnatal exposure to IPV is also linked to greater behavior problems in children, potentially due to the way that high-stress home environments can interfere with the development of self-regulation. Maternal sensitivity, on the other hand, is an important parenting factor that promotes children's adaptive self-regulation. papers.title: How alexithymia impacts the association between interpersonal trauma and somatization.
papers.abstract: Exposure to traumatic events has many health-related sequalae, one of which is somatization. Somatization is the manifestation of psychological or emotional distress in bodily symptoms, often leading to distressing thoughts and behaviors related to the physical symptoms and unusual or persistent requests for medical assistance. Interpersonal trauma, which includes traumatic events that occur in the context of an interpersonal relationship (e.g., physical/emotional/sexual assault, intimate partner violence, childhood trauma) has been strongly linked to somatic symptoms. Another potential risk factor for somatization is alexithymia, such that individuals with alexithymia struggle to understand their emotional distress and thus confuse it with bodily distress. The current study utilized secondary data analysis to investigate these constructs using a subset of items from the Traumatic Life Events Questionnaire, the somatization subscale of the Symptom Checklist-90 Revised, and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. It was hypothesized that higher ratings of interpersonal trauma would be associated with higher levels of somatization, and that this relationship would be moderated by levels of alexithymia. In a cross-sectional study of 531 young adults aged 18 to 29, interpersonal trauma and somatization demonstrated a small significant relationship (r = 0.178, p < 0.001), and the relationship between interpersonal trauma and somatization was moderated by alexithymia, β = 0.001, p = 0.027. The effect of interpersonal trauma on somatization was smaller when alexithymia was low (effect = 0.018) than the effect when alexithymia was high (effect = 0.043), showing that the relationship between trauma and somatization is stronger for individuals who have higher levels of alexithymia. papers.title: Cancer workforce readiness to identify and respond to domestic abuse: A national survey and follow-up interviews.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Domestic abuse (DA) is a highly prevalent public health and health equity issue. We aimed to investigate cancer professionals' experiences of DA among patients and assess cancer workforce readiness to identify, respond to, and prevent DA. METHODS: Cross-sectional survey (n = 343, mostly healthcare workers) and 15 follow-up interviews within an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. RESULTS: Most participants had encountered individuals affected by DA in the past three years. Participants often referred patients to cancer psychologists. Unique opportunities to respond to DA arose in the cancer pathway, including holistic psychosocial approaches to care. But alongside were unique challenges, including difficulties distinguishing DA from common emotional responses to cancer diagnoses. Inadequate training, policies, and private spaces for DA inquiry limited organizational readiness to respond. CONCLUSION: Carefully designed cancer-specific DA interventions are required to improve cancer professionals' confidence and knowledge to safely seize these unique opportunities to identify, respond to, and prevent DA.
